page: Microsoft Azure M128-64ms is a memory-intensive server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8280L processor operating at 2.7 GHz, configured with 32 physical cores and 64 virtual CPUs via Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The hardware profile includes a massive memory allocation of 3892.0 GB, yielding approximately 60.81 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 4194 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score, fall into the bottom 10% tier. Conversely, multi-threaded operations demonstrate average to strong capabilities. The bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and large-block memory bandwidth, both read and write, rank in the top 25%, indicating high efficiency for parallel memory-bound tasks. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks maintain average performance, while LLM text generation speeds remain poor.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a high-density memory resource. The high ratio of memory to compute makes it suitable for workloads that require massive RAM capacity but do not demand top-tier single-threaded CPU speeds. Tradeoffs include lower single-core performance relative to the overall hardware class. This configuration is suited for large in-memory databases, memory-intensive data processing, and parallelized multi-threaded workloads that can leverage the substantial memory bandwidth and large local storage.
